findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: The Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback now destructures the first destination calendar and reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration with no null check. destinationCalendar is often null or [] (no calendar connected, or the new array conversion produced an empty list). That throws TypeError before the booking is created, so a Google Meet event type with no destination calendar fails entirely instead of falling back to Cal Video. The previous optional chain (destinationCalendar?.integration) did not throw.

findings.title: Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: For collective events, other hosts' destination calendars are appended with evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). The array is initialized to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so optional chaining skips the push. Those hosts never get a calendar event, which is exactly the case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize an array before pushing, including when the organizer has no calendar.

findings.title: Office 365 always writes the first destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent still takes only the first element of destinationCalendar and ignores the credentialId that CalendarManager now passes. EventManager loops every collective host and calls createEvent with the full array plus that host's credential. Office 365 therefore creates every host's event on the first host's calendar (or the default calendar) and never on the other hosts' calendars. The same first-element-only pattern is in Lark (create/update/delete) and CalDAV, so non-Google collective hosts are not actually invited on their own calendars.

findings.title: Google organizer email is always the first host's calendar
findings.body: createEvent and updateEvent set the organizer attendee email from destinationCalendar[0].externalId, while the calendar written to is chosen by credentialId. For a collective booking each host's Google credential receives the same event, so secondary hosts' events list the first host's calendar id as organizer. Google can reject the insert, or the wrong person is marked organizer and the real host is only a guest. Use the destination entry whose credentialId matches the credential creating the event.

findings.title: Update/delete fallback search can never match a calendar
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent do destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). The right-hand side is null/undefined/empty, so the find never matches a real calendar id. Previously this path used destinationCalendar.externalId. Updates and deletes for bookings that have no stored externalCalendarId now hit an undefined calendarId (update) or silently fall back to "primary" (delete), so the event on the chosen calendar is not updated or removed. The hangout-link patch in createEvent has the same problem: it passes selectedCalendar without the || "primary" used by insert.

findings.title: Recurring cancel deletes only the first calendar reference, with every credential
findings.body: Inside the per-reference loop, cancelling all remaining recurring instances ignores the current reference and instead walks every user calendar credential, and for each updated booking only bookingRef = references.find(_calendar). Collective bookings now store one calendar reference per host, so only the first host's event is targeted, and it is deleted once per calendar credential (duplicate/wrong-credential deletes). Other hosts' recurring events are left on their calendars. Delete each updated booking's calendar references with the credential stored on that reference, as the non-recurring branch does.

findings.title: updateEvent is called when credential is still missing
findings.body: After the in-memory lookup and the DB fetch, updateAllCalendarEvents still pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) even if credential is undefined (no row, or app.slug missing so the fetch result is discarded). CalendarManager then calls getCalendar(undefined), the throw is caught, and every calendar reference in the batch is reported as failed. A single missing credential aborts updates for the other hosts instead of skipping that reference.

findings.title: Organization slug condition was inverted
findings.body: The org create payload changed from spreading slug when team billing is disabled (!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) to spreading slug only when billing is enabled. requestedSlug is still set when billing is enabled. With billing off, the new organization is created with no slug, so the org URL is never registered. With billing on, both slug and requestedSlug are set, which is the opposite of the previous split. This is unrelated to destination calendars and looks like an accidental boolean flip.
